item.title: 2020: A Year In Review
item.description: A reflection on a hard year, and the perspective it taught me.
item.content:encoded:
What a year this has been…

This article took me a lot of courage to write as I encountered so much negativity, toxicity, and despondency which heavily influenced my energy levels. In fact, as I try to focus on all the great things that happened this year, I cannot help myself but to shed tears from reminiscing the number of deaths I’ve encountered this year all the way to almost losing all my assets. Moreover, the drastic feeling of depression which led for me to gain 15 pounds in the span of a month and ignore the people that cares the most about me.

But, I also have learned how to shift my perspective and try to get the best out of a certain situation. I’ve learned how to reinvent myself so many times to adjust with the flow of the events. I’ve learned how to constantly improvise, overcome, and adapt.

When a photographer can’t change a scene, they either change their angles or their lens to capture the best of that scene. Similarly, when you cant change a situation in your life, change your perspective to get the best out of that situation.

Highlights

  • Interned with Oracle NetSuite and Dominion Energy which are both Fortune 100 companies
  • 4.0 GPA and certification in Financial Modelling and Valuation Analyst from Corporate Finance Institute and Business Analytics from Harvard Business School Online
  • Got invited for speaking opportunities and was featured in various magazines and newspaper!
  • Won 7 scholarships and represented Claflin University in more than 5 different virtual conferences!
  • Started a more hands-on approach in trading rather than passive investing!
  • Carved my first pumpkin and went to a pumpkin patch!
  • Learned how to cut my own hair and decorated my dorm room!
  • Helped 9 high school students get accepted to their dream universities with a full scholarship!
  • Got myself a new laptop fully funded by me!
  • Reconnecting with my Filipino Roots by reaching out to more Filipinos in the Philippines!

Virtual Summer Internship with Oracle and Dominion Energy

Having the opportunity to do a paid internship with Oracle as a Field Marketing Intern and Data Analyst with Dominion Energy is one of my biggest achievements in 2020. I can still remember when I was applying for different companies and was constantly rejected. I think that I applied to a total of 50 different internships and was only accepted to 10 of them.

Doing two virtual 40 hour internships over the summer with a pandemic going on was crazy. In addition to that, I was also located in PST when both of my internships was based in EST. Luckily, both of my managers were very accommodating and I was able to do my best at each of my internship and get an outstanding review of my performance.

In Oracle, I interned with the NetSuite Marketing team based in Denver, Colorado. As a Finance and Computer Science major, this was a step outside of my comfort zone as my main skills are in quantitative and technical analysis. However, I did gain a lot of qualitative skills as the President of two organizations during the school year at my university.

During the course of my internship, I worked within the intersection of sales and marketing by building productivity and customized tools to fill the gap and increase profits. I also built collaterals to help the Competitive Intelligence team provide actionable insights to executive members. For my final intern project, I created an in-depth presentation about how emerging technologies such as virtual reality and artificial intelligence can be utilized to radically enhance the ERP experience for consumers.

In Dominion Energy, it was a completely different experience compared to Oracle. I was with the Gas Development side as a Business Analyst and it was more of a technical experience. I developed an algorithm to effectively compare different forecasts of gas prices using tableau, excel, and a little bit of SQL. I also built a data map that consists of Dominion Energy assets that was utilized for managerial action and strategy of developing and acquiring other infrastructures. For my final project, I worked with a team of interns where we collaborated on improving the virtual onboarding process for the next group of interns.

It was also during this summer when the team that I was working with got acquired by Berkshire Hathaway and the Atlantic Coast Pipeline was cancelled. It was a learning moment for me since I get to witness how the acquisition was made and the changes that accompanied it. I’m really looking forward to see how Berkshire Hathaway plans to utilize their newly acquired assets in building more pipelines around the United States.

Certifications from Harvard Business School Online and Corporate Finance Institute + a 4.0 GPA

Prior to my sophomore year, I developed an interest on how to create financial models for businesses to utilize for better financial decisions.

Two months later, I was awarded with a generous financial aid from Corporate Finance Institute. However, as an undergraduate student with zero experience in financial modelling, I was unable to advance quickly as I made sure to embrace each topic presented and explored various ways on how I can apply it to my life.

After a year and a half, I have finally earned my Financial Modeling & Valuation Analyst Certification from Corporate Finance Institute. In addition, I was also selected as a CFI scholar! From budgeting and forecasting all the way to Excel VBA and modelling, I highly recommend this program to anyone interested in becoming a world-class financial analyst.

I also got a scholarship from Net Impact to take the Business Analytics course from Harvard Business School Online! This course completely changed my outlook in business as it exposed me to the importance of using data to make better managerial decisions! Before taking this course, my focus was mostly on compiling and gathering data. But, after this course, I learned so much about probabilities, statistics, A/B testing, and so much more.

It also introduced me to a global network of Filipinos who have taken their MBA at Harvard University. At first, it was very intimidating to network with them as I am still a student, but after doing a zoom session with them, I immediately felt like home and has always reached out to them whenever I needed help with anything!

Lastly, did I mentioned that I got a 4.0 this semester despite doing a virtual semester and waking up at 6am in the morning because I am in PST and my classes are at ET? It took me about not sleeping twice at night per week, but I was able to persevere and finish! Now, I am sleeping more than 12 hours per day during this winter break.

Claflin University → Zoom University

In the spring semester, when the Coronavirus was still not around, I served as the Campus Leader for the nationwide Up to Us competition. As a campus leader, I mobilized over 750 students at Claflin University to advocate for a sustainable fiscal future by creating an informative and creative campaign. We hosted game nights, movie shows, and a lot of other events to engage future leaders and educate them about the importance of being aware of the national debt and how it affects us in the future.

I was also the President for the Global Student Organization at Claflin University where we host various cultural activities to help promote global awareness in our campus community. We also do sessions to prepare international students for scholarships, internships, and any other concerns that are relevant within the international environment at my university.

For this semester, we were planning to do more events, but was abrupted due to the pandemic. However, we did have the first Henna event at Claflin University and had a lot of students who were more than happy to be a part of it!

Then, around March of 2020, Coronavirus became a thing. Universities have to shutdown and everything was moved to a virtual environment. As an out of state student, I was stuck in my university and it immediately became one of my darkest moments in life. My savings in the stock market from me working different jobs during my high school exponentially dropped. Six of my friends died due to an accident. I started stress eating and I gained 15 pounds in such a quick moment of time.

During the fall semester, I started remote learning while being based on a different time zone. It was very difficult to adjust, but I was able to overcome it by setting a healthy schedule on sleeping early and waking up early to start my day. I also learned the importance of getting enough time outside! At first, I was spending more than 15 hours in front of my computer. But, after having a severe headache, I started taking 20 minutes break for every 3 hours I spend working.

Expanding my Personal Brand

In 2019, I started a journey of improving my personal brand online and offline. I created my website and finally had the time to improve it this year after learning how to A/B test websites. I also was able to expand my LinkedIn followers to 3,000 this year! For 2021, I am aiming to reach 5,000 connections and make quality motivational posts rather than doing the traditional “I got accepted” posts!

In addition to having more than 3,000 connections in LinkedIn, I was also selected as one of the winners of the AICPA scholarships and was featured on their websites and magazine!

I can still remember when my teacher called me during one of our virtual class sessions and asked me if I have seen the South Carolina CPA Report Magazine. At first, I was confused because I really have not even heard about it before. But, when she told me that I was featured in it, I got really excited and made sure to get a copy as soon as possible.

I also served as one of the guest speakers for the first Up to Us Leadership Boot Camp this year! I mainly talked about how to embrace the new normal and how students can develop new skills that can not only be utilized for the Up to Us competition but on their day to day activities as well.

Investing + Fun Activities!

When the pandemic first started, the stock market massively plummeted and all I can think of was all my hard work going down the drain. At that time, all my assets were in the stock market and I did not have any remaining savings. The SPY index, which measures the performance of top 500 companies in the United States dropped from $338 to $222 in 1 month!

Therefore, I have decided to start a more hands-on approach in investing! I started learning about day trading, swing trading, and the pros and cons of different brokerages in regards with trading. I also started studying technical analysis of a certain stock and learning how major events can affect a stock performance.

In the end, I was able to gain a tremendous 488% increase in one week, but decided to take it a little bit easy because of the stress that comes along with it. During that week, I spent at least around 15 to 18 hours of researching different stocks and tracking the market per day.

Not only did I learned how to actively trade on the market, I also have decorated my dorm room with lights and connected it to my Alexa speaker! Every morning, I programmed my Alexa to wake me up at a certain time and it greets me by singing a new song every day! I can also tell Alexa to turn my lights on and off.

I also carved my first pumpkin this year and got a new laptop this year! This is the first time that I actually ordered a brand new laptop. In the previous years, I usually go with a refurbished one or buy a used one in eBay because it is cheaper and I know how to troubleshoot and fix laptops. The laptop that I got is a Dell XPS 15 9500. It is the 4K variant with 16GB of RAM, 512GB SSD, i7-10750H and a Nvidia GTX 1650 Ti. I mainly decided to go with this one because of the 16:10 aspect ratio which is very crucial for me as I plan to use this laptop for productivity and editing videos.

Plans for 2021?

I will be making a more in-depth article about my goals for 2021 but in summary, I plan to:

  • Publish 50 articles in Medium
  • Become more active on YouTube, Twitter, and Instagram and be more authentic in LinkedIn and Facebook!
  • Establish a social impact project in the Philippines! Impact over income!
  • Create a workout routine and consistently lose weight!
  • Finish 12 books
  • Schedule 5 coffee dates with friends every month

For 2021, my word of choice would be relationships! I am aiming for a year of friendships, new people, and nurturing relationships. After all, strangers are just friends waiting to meet.

Huge shoutout to all the people and family who stick with me till the end of this year! Special shoutout to the new people I met through reddit, Quora, Facebook, and especially Tinder! I would not be where I am right now if it were not for you all!

item.title: Internship at Oracle Amidst a Global Pandemic
item.description: Lessons from a remote summer as a Field Marketing intern at Oracle NetSuite.
item.content:encoded:
Our economy is changing daily, and with it, the talents, skills and experience needed to rapidly adapt of that growth cycle are too. The job market is very competitive, and a tough learning curve for recent graduates. This is why experiential learning and applying to internships are important along with the college experience for all students.

During the summer of 2020, amidst a global pandemic, I had the opportunity to intern at Oracle NetSuite as a Field Marketing Intern working on the intersection of sales and marketing line of business.

I was very excited to start my journey in Corporate America, but at the same time, I was very anxious. It was during a time of uncertainty due to the pandemic, and I am not sure what to expect. However, I accepted the offer with an open mind and willingness to learn and, it was the most productive summer of my life!

I brainstormed on what I really want to achieve from this internship, and I had 3 main goals in mind:

  • Understand how Oracle NetSuite revolutionized the traditional legacy systems with data driven solutions to enable businesses to make better decisions.
  • Empathize why businesses need an Enterprise Resource Planning System to scale their business even farther.
  • Network, Network, Network!

Looking back at the past ten weeks, I was able to achieve all these goals and so much more! I was very pleased with my experience and would not trade anything for it! Here are some key lessons that I learned during this summer!

Step Out Of Your Comfort Zone! Do Not Hesitate!

In college, I was known for my excel and analytical skills which helped me stood out especially during business competitions or a project that requires financial modelling. But, I was also known for having terrible design skills, knowledge of wider business context and for presentation and reporting skills. (Guess you just can’t have it all!)

Therefore, when I learned that my role is going to be about researching and developing marketing programs to help increase customer engagement, I was very nervous. I never had any experience with that, let alone any knowledge about it.

I approached this problem with transparency and an open mind. Right at the beginning of my internship, I told my manager that I don’t have any experience working with marketing or sales, but at the same time, I emphasized that I am more than willing to learn and have done various leadership experiences which helped me developed transferable skills.

Now, after 10 weeks, I can confidently talk about the general business outlook of different industries, effectively present materials to executives, and most of all, be able to utilize excel spreadsheets integrated with data and use it to make better business decisions!

Pro tip: Take advantage of the learning resources! Most companies have a platform specific for developing and learn new skill sets! This is a great way for you to get out of your comfort zone and maybe learn about coding or some new software!

Finding Impact Within Your Work

Having an impact is one of the most fulfilling experiences you can ever have as an intern. It can either be qualitative or quantitative proof that your work was useful and helped with the company’s mission and vision.

Just think about it, you’re bringing a new perspective on the products compared to someone who might be working on it for 5+ years.

However, be realistic about achieving impact from a short time-frame. Most changes or deliverable to get published takes time. There are countless design and development review cycles to ensure that the product delivers the intended value to specific audience. That is why it is important to remember that impact can be measured in so much more ways! (You don’t have to create a new supply chain process to revolutionize the company’s production!)

Here are some examples:

  • Did your work helped the team to automate some manual tasks such as by developing templates for sending out emails, making power points, or even creating a guidebook for new interns?
  • Were you able to have discussions with different employees and introduced random new ideas and get them thinking? Ask a lot of questions!!
  • Learn more about the company! Companies invest in interns not for the value they provide during the internship but for the potential value if they come back to the firm!

Overall, interns can add value by learning, doing a great job on what they are assigned, asking questions, and by not being a liability!

Pro tip: Go to meetings! Even if it is not with your team! You never know when you can make a suggestion or ask a random question that will make them think and reinforce new decisions that can drive change within the business!

Who knows, maybe you can even suggest a future feature of a certain product and you can get dibs on it!

Network, Network, Network!

Internships are one of the best ways to explore a company’s culture and its different line of businesses. Even though I was working on marketing and sales, I was very passionate about finance, business analytics, venture capital, and private equity. I immediately told my manager that I wanted to learn more about Oracle’s approach in helping startups, marketing analytics, global and its finance team.

Having this discussion during the start of my internship allowed us to tailor a timeline to meet different employees every week.

Thankfully, my manager was very adaptive and she took the time out of her busy schedule to ensure that I was able to meet with different business segments and help out with any projects to get a feel on what are the day to day responsibilities working within that role.

Fun fact: I was able to connect with an Oracle employee from the Philippines, my hometown! Also, Jollibee is a client of NetSuite! Yum!

Working Hard Independently

Do not watch Netflix during your work times. Again, do not watch Netflix during your working hours. Do I need to say more?

In conclusion, despite working remotely, my summer at Oracle helped me gain more insight about the importance of finance and analytics in marketing. It also made me realize that having qualitative skills to go along with my excel skills will help me a long way as I climb the ropes within the financial industry. Big thanks to the Oracle Intern program and UNCF for helping students have an amazing experience despite everything that’s going on in the world.

Disclaimer: The opinions expressed in this article are those of the author. They do not necessarily reflect the opinions or views of Oracle or its employees.

item.title: 3 Advices On Creating A Credible Investment Thesis
item.description: What my HBCUvc fellowship taught me about building an investment thesis.
item.content:encoded:
As a HBCUvc Fellow, I have been exposed in the field of venture capital constantly. Here are some tips on how to construct an investment thesis without having to stay up all night and trying to cram all your scattered thoughts in a pitch deck.

Just recently, as my colleagues and I were having a discussion on creating our investment thesis, we had difficulties in navigating through different industries and finding one that appeals to us the most and one that creates the most revenue for further development.

As a Finance and Computer Science major, my focus was creating a thesis that revolves around the E-learning industry because it utilizes technology and as we all know, technology is the future.

In fact, the industry of e-learning is expected to reach $325 billion by 2025! That’s a no brainer, right? After all, one of the main goals of an investment thesis is to generate profit so they can stay in the business! But, my colleagues were more focused on basing our model on something that is more scalable and realistic. Eventually, we reached a decision.

Here are the main three lessons that I learned during our call as we form our investment thesis.

1. Focus on making an impact compared to generating revenue

I can never forget the time when my colleague was describing her investment thesis and all I can think of was money, revenue, and the cost that we need to incur to make it happen. It’s like I am already thinking on when we will reach break-even and start generating profit when we are still unsure on what is our main idea is about.

“How in the world are we going to generate revenue from this project?”

In fact, to be honest, I was not even listening to her idea until she talked about the numbers. Eventually, as we talked more and got deeper on the projected impact of her business model, I realized that an investment thesis should not be so focused on generating revenue on the short run. First, it should be about initiating change and making an impact to the community. Then, the money will eventually come as long it is making constant development in people’s lives. It’s like planting a seed in a forest. It takes years to grow but; it is worth it especially once it bears fruit.

2. Pick an industry you are passionate with, not where the money is at

Writing an investment thesis can be very hard especially if you still don’t know what type of industry to pursue. You might want to focus in early stage/start ups or you want something with lesser risk such as jumping into a developed market. Additionally, it might also be very tempting to enter the realm of technology because of its growth, innovation, and it is widely implemented. However, you must also be aware that there will be a lot of different groups that have this same mindset.

Yes, money is important after all, that makes the business run. However, investment thesis is not just a temporary plan. It is a game plan that will serve as the main components of your VC that will answer the 5 W’s (who, what, why, when, where). Therefore, you would want to have something that you believe in and try to find an opportunity for growth within that industry.

Ultimately, the best advice I have for you is to brainstorm, as a group, and ask yourselves some questions about your identity, your background, and your interests. Then, using those informations, try to come up with an industry that everyone is passionate about because it reflects your identity or a moment in life that defines you and your journey in life. Next, once you determine the type of industry that you would want to focus on, it will lead to my last and final advice which is…

3. Creativity is Key to Success!

Last but not the least, I cannot emphasize enough on the importance of creativity. Creativity drives Innovation which leads to Growth. It’s because of creative minds that we have hybrid vehicles, smartphones, tablets, and even artificial intelligence! Who knows? You might be the next person to invest in a company that manufactures the next flying vehicles or maybe something simple as Tinder for Pets that uses sound recognition to swipe :P

Final Thoughts

Hopefully, these tips can make an impact as you develop your own investment thesis. If you would like to add something on the list, please do not hesitate to reach out! Looking forward on hearing more from you.

item.title: 2019: The Year in Review
item.description: Studying abroad, starting FMU Photography, and a year of stepping out of my comfort zone.
item.content:encoded:
2019 has been an incredible year full of stepping out of my comfort zone, meeting new friends, and having more experiences! In fact, I can still vividly remember when I studied abroad in United Kingdom last summer, not knowing what lies ahead of me. 2019 has also been a year full of cultivating self-realization, self-discovery, and self-awareness. This is my first time writing an end of year review as well! Let’s jump to the highlights!

Highlights

  • Studied abroad in London, England with a full scholarship as a Frederick Douglass Global Fellow!
  • Established my own photography business (FMU Photography).
  • Won a Hackathon and a Business Plan Competition.
  • Attended 12 different conferences representing Claflin University.
  • Attended the National Fiscal Summit at Washington DC and met policymakers along with Nancy Pelosi and other congressional leaders.
  • Visited 18 states in the United States all paid by different companies.
  • Served as a Luard Morse Ambassador promoting the importance of Historically Black Universities in the community and the United Methodist Church.
  • Finished 2 different research proposals and presented it in various research symposiums.
  • Did I mention that I also got a brand new guitar and an electric guitar? :P

Studying Abroad in London, England

Last March, I can still remember when I got a call from the Center of International Education Exchange saying that I got accepted as a Frederick Douglass Global Fellow. It has been the most amazing experience that I had in the whole year, in fact, maybe my whole life! I got to travel in London, England with a full scholarship where I met ten other fellows and we literally stayed together the whole time and formed memories that will last us for a lifetime.

My most memorable memory happened around 2 am. As a photographer, I love taking pictures at night. I was busy admiring the dazzling scenery full of lit buildings, when all of a sudden, my phone began to ring and I saw that my phone is around 6%. Not knowing what to do, I texted my cohort my location and asking them to pick me up, although really, it was a joke. I know that there is no way they are still awake, let alone leave their comfy beds in the middle of the morning just to get this guy who they barely knew for a month.

But, all of a sudden, the next thing I know, I can hear their voices. Their loud shouts filling the empty streets of Westminster.

Travelling to Belfast, Ireland and Edinburgh, Scotland

During my time at United Kingdom, my cohort was also granted the opportunity to visit Belfast, Ireland where we learned about the role that Northern Ireland have in the potential event that has been going on for so long. You guessed it… Brexit.

Belfast is a really great place that is full of heartwarming stories and streets that speaks memories to you as you walk by, looking at the portraying images on the walls. Oh yeah, we visited the congressional building, Titanic museum, and the freedom wall! But, most of all, we went hiking! Wew! Another step outside of my own comfort zone!!

On the last week of July, my friends and I were planning of going to Paris, because duhh, we were already in United Kingdom and like the plane ticket is only around $150.00. Unfortunately, since I was still a green card holder, and I didn’t have the right visa to enter Europe, I was not able to go with them. It was a very sad moment, but Daniela Quinones, a FDGF fellow also, and I decided to go to Edinburgh, Scotland instead.

It was still a very fun trip, the accent of Scottish people are so hard to understand that we were literally just nodding our head when we went to restaurants or our AirBnbs. Yep, you guessed it, we did more hiking!! Another step outside of my comfort zone!

Professional Development and Conferences Attended

During the school year, I was very privileged to be selected by various companies to represent my university at professional development conferences. It was great having to see role models and professionals who were so willing to volunteer and speak at these conferences and continuing to inspire students. A few of the conferences that I attended includes:

  • DHG and UNC Chapel Hill Accounting Mentorship Program
  • Kelley School of Business Accounting Weekend
  • National Fiscal Summit 2019
  • National Diversity Leadership Summit
  • HBCU Venture Capital Fall Retreat
  • Deloitte HBCU Emerging Leaders Conference
  • Dominion Energy Conference

Additionally, it was very cool to see Nancy Pelosi in action during the National Fiscal Summit! It was very intense to witness political backfiring conversations and learning how to respond effectively! Ooof! Talk about stepping out of my comfort zone!

Leadership and Volunteer Experiences

Not only 2019 was a year full of catching flights to different conferences for free, it was also a year full of community service, volunteering, and leadership development!

I was elected as the President of Global Student Organization where I had the opportunity to represent the international students at Claflin University and hold events that promotes cultural awareness. I was also the Outreach Leader for Net Impact’s Up to Us Competition where my team and I mobilized over 500 students on my campus to advocate for a sustainable fiscal future by creating an informative and creative campaign. I also served as the Fundraising Chair for National Association of Black Accountants and a general member of National Society of Black Engineers. Just recently, I was also selected as a HBCU Venture Capital Fellow where I get to receive hands on training from skilled venture professionals, in the hope of advocating entrepreneurship in minority serving institutions.

Hackathons, Case Competitions, and Research Symposium

In addition to my travels and involvement in my community as a student leader, I was also very fortunate to win several awards at different academic competitions!

As my parents always say “Never forget about your academics while you are in college!”

During early January, my team and I entered a Hackathon at Clemson University, CUHackIt. It was my first exposure to the realm of Computer Science and I was so fascinated on how we can create different software to solve a problem, which led for me to double major in Computer Science and Finance!

Fun fact: My team won the best beginner award!

In 2019, I also led a team of talented students to enter our first business plan competition! It was a very tedious process that involves a lot of financial analysis, making comprehensive business models, and researching various industries. Then, we presented our idea to a panel of well-established market leaders and CEO of different startup companies!

Fun fact: This was our first time of entering a business plan competition and we won 2nd place with prize money of $3,000! Definitely not bad for our first time!

Lastly, but not the least, I was also fortunate enough to represent my institution, Claflin University at the HBCU Battle of the Brains. Even though we did not win this time, I am more than excited to be a part of it again.

Photography Business

When I was in 12th grade, my friends have always told me that I have an eye for detail. They constantly told me that I should be a photographer and they will wholeheartedly support me.

As usual, being my stubborn self, I did not listen to them until this year, where I actually launched my own photography business, FMU Photography.

I started doing photography for fun since 2016 and have always loved it. But, now, I decided to take another step out of my comfort zone and actually start professionally taking pictures! So far, I am very pleased to say that I had more than 30 clients on my first year and I am looking forward for another year of growth, prosperity, and success!

Lastly, I would just like to express my biggest gratitude to my family, friends, and my Tinder, Bumble, and Hinge dates who have supported me to be the person I am today. Oh yeah, special mention to my cuddly teddy bears who are always there for me :P

item.title: Conferences and Events for Latinx Student Entrepreneurs
item.description: Why building connections matters, and four events worth attending.
item.content:encoded:
Back in my younger years, I never emphasized on cultivating connections. Growing up alone, most of the times, I can pretty much do everything by myself.

“What is the point of working with other people? It usually means more work because they have to agree with my ideas.”

However, that all changed when I went to high school at Spanaway Lake High School in Spanaway, Washington. I was exposed to so many people with different backgrounds that I gradually realized that differing and conflicting opinions are significant to form an innovative idea.

As an aspiring entrepreneur and investor, forming connections is very crucial to consolidate my network. I can still remember when I traveled to Tijuana, Mexico where I encountered so many students and professionals with brilliant ideas that can change the world (yes, I am not kidding!) but does not have the resources to do so. They don’t even know the definition of venture capitals, let alone angel investors.

Thus, it came to my attention that there are many Latinx networking events where entrepreneurs, business owners, and innovators come together to learn from each other. It is a huge networking event that everyone should take advantage of. More importantly, if you are a student, they usually have HUGE discounts just for you! So, what are you waiting for? Go ahead and apply! Below are just some of them:

P.S. If you have any recommendations that I should include, please don’t hesitate to send me a message! I will be more than happy to collaborate with you.

1. PortadaLat

  • Location: Miami, Florida
  • Dates: June 8–9
  • Prices: Varies

Through a morning of bespoke workshops and pre-scheduled 1:1 meetings, an afternoon of open conference sessions and a fun evening, PortadaLat will provide attendees an ideal platform to gain new business and entrepreneurial intelligence. It’s a two-day annual gathering of key brand marketing, advertising, media and content leaders from all over the Americas.

2. Latina Think Big Innovation Summit

  • Location: San Francisco, CA
  • Dates: October 6
  • Prices: Free

This one day event showcases the innovative ideas and talents of Latina, in a series of short talks. These talks bring successful leaders, tech entrepreneurs, and cultivators together in an environment that fosters connection and education.

3. Association of Latino Professionals for America (ALPFA Convention)

  • Location: Nashville, TN
  • Dates: August 3 – August 6
  • Prices: $1,550 or $250 for students (LOTS OF SCHOLARSHIPS AVAILABLE!)

The ALPFA National Convention is a truly special experience for students and professionals alike. Thousands of purpose-driven Latinos will gather for a week of learning, networking, and professional growth. Their corporate partners are waiting to meet talented individuals like you! This is a great event that I have personally seen, and it is highly recommended by all of my peers.

4. Forbes Under 30

  • Location: Varies
  • Dates: October 25–28
  • Prices: $400 (You can find a lot of discounts online! It can be as low as $35 for students)

I am sure you have heard of Forbes!! It’s a very well known event that encompasses networking, trade shows, top playlists, innovation, healthcare, and successful entrepreneurs! It is more than an immersive experience than a static conference: a private music festival, A-list speakers, investor speed-pitching, industry-focused field trips, a legendary pub crawl, a world-famous food festival and a powerful day of community service.

Please do note that the location, dates, and prices varies. These data are gathered from the year 2019.
